one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window to 2026-11-12: Texas Instruments Q3 results on Wed 2026-10-21 (call 3:30pm CT, source 30), the first read on analog/industrial demand and pricing, and ST's own Q3 results on 2026-10-29 before the European open (call 9:30 CET, sources 5, 31, 17). Q3 is guided at $3.70B and 37% GM with Q4 already said to be above $4B (source 2), so the swing factor is the Q4 margin guide and any 2027 framing. Our lane's data lean mildly positive (three 2026 price hikes, auto MCUs +15-20%, 30-52 week power lead times per TrendForce, source 7; SiC substrate prices bottoming and NXP channel inventory a normal 11 weeks per PCIM, source 10), but ST's recent earnings-day reactions were large and mostly negative (Q2 'slump', source 15), and these signals are public. With two events and 61% realized vol (17.4% a month), we use a ~19% one-month spread, centred a touch below spot ($49.3 median) rather than taking a directional view; no other company event is scheduled (CEO reappointment, source 4, is neutral).

fair_value.method: Engine blend of a 10.4%-WACC DCF ($44.51, 40%) and 17x NTM GAAP after-SBC EPS of ~$3.09 at the horizon ($52.46, 60%), on consensus revenue ($14.43B FY26, $17.17B FY27), GAAP EBIT 7.5%/15%/19.5%/20%, guided 2026 capex at 15.2% of revenue, net cash $1,701M less $406M minorities, 910.7M diluted shares.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue FY26 $14.43B, FY27 $17.17B, FY28 $18.37B, FY29 $19.11B; GAAP EBIT 7.5%/15%/19.5%/20%; tax 18%/17%; capex 15.2%/13%/11.5%/11%; D&A 13.2%-10.7%; NWC 15% of incremental revenue; WACC 10.4%; g 3%; net cash $1,701M, minorities $406M; 910.7M shares -0.5%/yr

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY26 revenue $14.43B / FY25 $11.80B - 1 = 22.3%. Cross-check: Q1 $3.095B + Q2 $3.487B + Q3 guide $3.70B + Q4 'above $4B' = ~$14.3B+.

Consensus FY27 $17.18B / $14.43B - 1 = 19.0%. Round 1 added 1pt for 2026 price hikes and lead times; the supervisor discounted the blog part of that and the verified TrendForce data (three hikes, auto MCUs +15-20%, 30-52 week power lead times) is already visible to the street, so it now sits in the bull scenario, not the base. Q4'26 guide above $4B x 4 = $16B+ supports consensus.
Growth slows as the cycle matures; FY28 ~$18.4B is just above the 2023 peak $17.29B (F1). The 2023-25 fall of 32% (F1 to F3) after the 2021-22 lead-time spike is why we do not extend high growth.

H1 GAAP operating income $70M + $187M = $257M on $6.58B revenue (3.9%). H2 revenue = FY26 consensus $14.43B - $6.58B = $7.85B. Q3: guided $3.70B x 37% GM = $1.37B gross profit less ~$1.03B GAAP opex at Q2's level (Q2: 3,487 x 34.8% - 187 = $1,026M) = ~$0.34B (9.3%); Q4 (above $4B) higher, so H2 ~10.5% = ~$0.82B. FY26: ($0.257B + $0.82B) / $14.43B = 7.5%. (At an H2 margin of 11% the year would be 7.8%.)
inputs_detail.citation_gate_fix: citation gate 2026-10-14: the shown arithmetic (H2 ~11%) gave 7.8%, not 7.5%; derivation corrected to the H2 margin (~10.5%) that gives the stated 7.5%

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY27 EPS $2.69 (after SBC; ST non-GAAP excludes only restructuring and NXP-MEMS PPA) x ~911M shares = ~$2.45B net income; / (1 - 17%) = ~$2.95B pre-tax = ~17.2% of $17.17B; less ~2pts of restructuring/PPA that GAAP keeps (Q2: $58M + $24M a quarter = ~$330M/yr) = ~15%.

FY2023 GAAP operating margin 26.7% (F5 $4,611M / F1 $17,286M). Less ~2.4pts for higher D&A ($1,854M in FY25 vs $1,561M in FY23, F21/F19, on similar revenue), ~2pts for Power & Discrete still loss-making (Q2 operating loss $99M) after the SiC price war (PCIM), and ~2-3pts because Q3 GM is guided at only 37% vs ~48% in 2023. FY2026 18%: ST's guided 2026 estimated annual effective rate 18.1% before discrete items incl. ~0.5pt Pillar Two (Q2 OFR; 19.3% actual 2025). FY2027 on 17%: agent estimate, not guidance (ST gives no rate beyond 2026): a judgment between the 18.1% guide and FY24's 16.7% (313/1,878; FY23 11.4% = 541/4,763), with Pillar Two as a floor. The supervisor's reconciled set uses 18% in every year.

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 2026 D&A $946M (OFR cash-flow statement) -> ~$1.9B FY26 / $14.43B = 13.2%; then D&A rising ~$50M a year ($1.95B, $2.0B, $2.05B) on the revenue path.

FY26: net capex guided 'in the high end of the $2.0 to $2.2 billion range' (Q2 OFR) -> $2.2B / FY26 revenue $14.43B (consensus) = 15.2% (guided $ amount, derived %; round 1 wrongly annualised H1's $771M to 12%). FY25 net capex was $1,844M (15.6% of revenue) and FY24 $2,642M (19.9%). FY27-29 have no company guidance: agent estimate, capex modulated toward D&A as reshaping ends, slightly above D&A for datacenter optics capacity: 13% x $17.17B = $2.23B, 11.5% x $18.38B = $2.11B, 11% x $19.11B = $2.10B.

Cost of equity 5.24% (DGS10 2026-10-09) + Blume beta 1.32 (0.67 x raw 1.48 + 0.33) x 4.20% implied ERP (Damodaran, 2026-10-01) = 10.78%. Debt ~$3.27B (Q2 financial debt $4.02B less $750M Tranche B repaid) vs $43.78B market cap = 7% weight, at 6.25% pre-tax (rf + ~1pt for a Baa1/BBB+ issuer, judgment) x (1 - 17%) = 5.2%. 0.93 x 10.78% + 0.07 x 5.2% = 10.4%.
Nominal growth for analog/MCU/power content in autos, industry and datacenter after FY2029; long-dated risks (cycle, SiC, Apple) keep it at 3%, not higher.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17x NTM GAAP after-SBC EPS: at the 16.6x core median as quoted, and ~3-6% below it once peers' SBC add-back is removed (~17.5-18x). STM today is ~18.4x FY27 consensus ($49.57 / $2.69).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. The small discount on a like-for-like basis rests on structural, persistent gaps: GAAP operating margin 1.5% in FY25 (F7/F3) and a 37% Q3 GM guide vs ~57-64% at TXN/NXPI/MCHP; capital intensity (2026 net capex ~15% of revenue, D&A 15.7% of FY25 revenue, F21/F3); 17.7% customer concentration in Apple (20-F). Datacenter growth (well above $2B in 2027) and a net-cash balance sheet stop it from going lower, toward NXPI's 12.45x.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$31 (about 10x our horizon NTM GAAP EPS of ~$3.09 and 11.5x FY27 consensus $2.69, ~37% below spot, above the $26 bear value) the market would be pricing a failed recovery rather than ordinary volatility in a 61%-vol stock: the 2026 price hikes and long lead times turned into double-ordering and cancellations, the 'well above $2B' 2027 datacenter target was withdrawn, Q4 fell short of the >$4B guide, or margins stalled near 10% despite ~$16B revenue.

catalysts.event: Texas Instruments Q3 2026 results: read on analog/industrial demand and pricing
ST Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide (Q3 guided $3.70B / 37% GM; Q4 said above $4B)
Supplier price-increase rounds and distributor lead-time updates (TrendForce/Findchips/Accuris): whether tight supply persists
Q4 2026 results and FY2027 framework incl. capex plan and datacenter confirmation
Q1 2027 results; whether pricing holds after inventory rebuild
AGM incl. one-year CEO reappointment; succession visibility

key_uncertainties: Whether the 2026 shortage (three ST price hikes, 30-52 week lead times) is end demand or double-ordering like 2021-22, which ended in a 32% revenue fall (F1 to F3)
Delivery of the AI datacenter ramp (>$1B in 2026, well above $2B in 2027)
Gross margin recovery: Q3 guide 37% vs ~48% in 2023; unused-capacity charges and reshaping costs
Power & Discrete losses (Q2 operating loss $99M) and whether SiC substrate prices keep recovering after the price war
Rates: 10y at 5.24% and a 1.48 raw beta make the multiple sensitive to the discount rate
CEO succession: the reappointment is for one year only

reverse_dcf_check: The engine says the 17x NTM P/E implies a 9.3% WACC on our cash flows vs our 10.4%, i.e. the multiple leg ($52.5) is richer than the DCF ($44.5). Holding 10.4%, 17x needs either ~4.2% perpetual growth after FY2029 or a ~23% steady-state GAAP EBIT margin (vs our 20% and 26.7% at the 2023 peak, F5/F1); we checked both on the engine (g 4.3% gives a $53.0 DCF; a 23.2% FY29 margin gives $51.2). That is achievable in a good cycle but not the median outcome once the down-cycle, SiC, Apple and datacenter risks above are counted, which is why the DCF keeps 40% weight and the multiple stays at or below the core peer median.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC $193M (F25). The model uses GAAP EBIT after SBC (1.5% of revenue). ST's non-GAAP EPS excludes only restructuring/impairment and NXP-MEMS PPA, not SBC (Q2 2026 reconciliation), so consensus EPS is also after SBC. Peers' adjusted EPS adds SBC back, so their quoted P/Es are ~5-10% low versus ST's basis; we allow for that in the 17x. Shares fall only 0.5%/yr net, so SBC is not counted again as dilution.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks hold and cut my fair value from $55.2 to $49.3. (1) Discount rate: my 4.99% was the September GS10 average; daily DGS10 is 5.24% (9 Oct) and I had no source for beta ~1.0. Rebuilt from sources: Blume beta 1.32 from raw 1.48, Damodaran's 4.20% implied ERP (1 Oct), 7% debt -> 10.4% (supervisor 10.6% with a 4.5% ERP; I use the sourced 4.2%). (2) New from the Q2 OFR, which the supervisor did not flag: 2026 net capex is guided at the high end of $2.0-2.2B, i.e. 15.2% of revenue, not the 12% I annualised from H1; 2026 tax is guided at 18.1%; noncontrolling interest is $406M (I had 0). (3) Shares: the diluted-EPS table is 890.15M basic + 7.70M awards + 12.80M customer warrants + 17.31M convert shares; removing only the convert shares gives 910.7M (supervisor ~900M; I keep the warrants, which are real dilution). (4) FY28-29 GAAP margins cut from 21/21.5% to 19.5/20%: the 37% Q3 GM guide and 15.7% D&A do not support 21%. (5) FY27 growth back to the +19% consensus; the verified TrendForce pricing data go into the bull case, and the Lifeboat blog, Digitimes headline and keyed SOXX figure are gone. (6) Peers: MCHP corrected to 16.19x, ALGM put on next-FY EPS (22.7x), MPWR/SLAB out of the median -> core median 16.6x, so 17x stays. The engine gives DCF $44.5 (40%) and P/E $52.5 (60%) = $49.3, roughly flat to the $49.57 close; scenarios $26 / $49 / $69 at 25/50/25. Ladder: lognormal around a ~$49 median with ~47-50% annual spread (below the 61% realized vol, which includes the June spike and fall, but above the 42% the scenario mixture alone implies) and a slightly fat left tail for the cycle risk; P(>= spot) just under 0.5.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY26 revenue $14.43B / FY25 $11.80B - 1 = 22.3%. Cross-check: Q1 $3.095B + Q2 $3.487B + Q3 guide $3.70B + Q4 'above $4B' = ~$14.3B+.

Consensus FY27 $17.18B / $14.43B - 1 = 19.0%. Round 1 added 1pt for 2026 price hikes and lead times; the supervisor discounted the blog part of that and the verified TrendForce data (three hikes, auto MCUs +15-20%, 30-52 week power lead times) is already visible to the street, so it now sits in the bull scenario, not the base. Q4'26 guide above $4B x 4 = $16B+ supports consensus.
Growth slows as the cycle matures; FY28 ~$18.4B is just above the 2023 peak $17.29B (F1). The 2023-25 fall of 32% (F1 to F3) after the 2021-22 lead-time spike is why we do not extend high growth.

H1 GAAP operating income $70M + $187M = $257M on $6.58B revenue (3.9%). H2 revenue = FY26 consensus $14.43B - $6.58B = $7.85B. Q3: guided $3.70B x 37% GM = $1.37B gross profit less ~$1.03B GAAP opex at Q2's level (Q2: 3,487 x 34.8% - 187 = $1,026M) = ~$0.34B (9.3%); Q4 (above $4B) higher, so H2 ~10.5% = ~$0.82B. FY26: ($0.257B + $0.82B) / $14.43B = 7.5%. (At an H2 margin of 11% the year would be 7.8%.)
